evidence.requirements: Met: the start page has the heading, Search, Family select, count, name links and L3 (list.jpg; app.js:108-170). Search treats comma and point alike (search.js:21-34). Detail facts, capacity with source link, grouped Symbol/Value/Unit tables, Print, All cartridges and hash addresses are all present (app.js:172-287). The drawing rules are coded in geometry.js. Partly met or unmet: (1) Diameters R1, P1, P2, H1, H2, G1, E1 are single-arrow leaders from the upper outline to a shelf (layout.js:222-235). They are not dimension lines with arrowheads at both ends and extension lines, as the reference drawings show. (2) The α arc is centred on apex S and sweeps only α/2 from the axis (layout.js:240-255). For 9,3 x 74 R, S = 113.17 lies past the tip (L6 96.5), so the arc and the 'α 10°58'00"' label float in empty space (detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg). On 308 the arc lies over the bullet (detail-308_win.jpg). (3) Print does not show the drawing at full width: the whole sheet is scaled to about 55% of the page width (print-308_win.jpg; app.js:279-283). (4) The title block always says 'Scale 1:1' (layout.js:300), but the screen scale is several times larger.
evidence.correctness: geometry.js follows the rules closely: rim classification (59-66); chamfer min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (302-306); rimfire half-round (287-294); groove and belt ramp at δ to R3/2 (322-345); body, shoulder with tangent fillets r1 min and r2 (361-380); tangent ogive with correct ρ and centre (180-187); quarter ellipse; cones; seating s and k tables (137-151); heeled H2 and H2-2tb (169-177); tn/tb, linear blend across the shoulder (415-421); w terms (407-411); pocket sizes and depths (19-27). The computed apex for 308 equals S = 55.46. Values are printed as published (format.js:66-73) and tolerances sit in the same cell ('39.62 -0.2' in detail-308_win.jpg). The profile proportions in detail-308_win.jpg and detail-300_win_mag.jpg match the reference drawings. Defects: the α arc spans the half-angle but is labelled with the included angle, and is placed off the part. The 'Scale 1:1' claim is false. The diameters are leaders, not true diameter dimensions. The print fits one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg), but only by scaling the sheet and clipping with .print-fit overflow:hidden, against a hand-calibrated height estimate (styles.css:326-335; app.js:56-66).
evidence.security: Only the SVG string goes through innerHTML (app.js:255). In it, every text and aria-label is escaped by esc() (svg.js:16-22, 54, 63, 90), the numbers come from num(), and the hatch id is sanitised (svg.js:59). Everything else uses textContent and createElement (app.js:81-97). There is no eval, no fetch and no external assets (index.html). Capacity URLs are plain anchors with rel=noopener.
evidence.code_quality: The modules are small and pure (format, search, geometry, layout, svg, app) with a UMD wrapper so Node tests can load them. Names are clear and missing values produce notes. Leftovers: legAxis is built but never drawn (layout.js:256); there is a one-element candidate loop (layout.js:267); the comment says 'Two columns' above columns: 3 (styles.css:350-352). Print fit depends on magic calibration constants (app.js:59-64).
evidence.tests: Six node:test files. They cover rim types, chamfer, the rimfire half-round, groove and belt ramp angle, the shoulder half-angle and apex, fillets, missing r1 min, the straight case, all bullet shapes with s/k/m, ogive and ellipse point checks, the heeled bullet, walls, w, primer pockets, missing-value notes, label overlap and outline overlap for all 25 records, title block, formatting, tolerances, symbols, units, search and routes. Gaps: there is no browser or DOM test (rendering, print being one page, keyboard). The α label check did not catch the off-part placement, and the print-height test is only a calibrated estimate.
evidence.ux_design: The facts list is dense and readable. The drawing reads as a technical drawing with hatched section and centre line. Weaknesses: dimension labels are very large next to the part (3.2 mm text on a 9 mm case, detail-9_mm_luger.jpg), and the title block is bigger than the drawing (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). The 22 LR 'L3 15.57' label is pushed left of the head, away from its line. The floating α on 9,3 x 74 R is confusing. Tables are single-column, full-width and very long (4700 px for 308), and the Value column x-position changes from table to table. In print, the drawing is not full width and the tables are scaled to about 4 pt (print-308_win.jpg). There is no dark-mode screenshot; the CSS supports dark mode.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img with aria-label '<name> drawing' (svg.js:63). Tables have th scope=col, and sections have h3 headings and aria-label (app.js:201-231). Search and Family have labels (app.js:140-141), the count is aria-live (134), and there is a skip link and :focus-visible outlines (styles.css:72-86). Focus moves to main on route change and inputs are 44 px targets. Muted text #5b6370 on #fbfbf9 has adequate contrast. Lacks: no long description of the drawing beyond its name, and no table captions.
evidence.simplicity: About 1,300 lines of plain JS and CSS, no runtime dependencies and no dev dependencies; node:test is built in. The structure fits the problem. The one avoidable complexity is the estimated-height scale-and-clip print mechanism.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, no CI configuration, no ADRs and no docs explaining setup or decisions. The OpenSpec specs (openspec/specs/*) document behaviour well, and `npm test` exists. The Node version is only engines '>=22' (no .nvmrc). The version is 1.0.0 with no release approach. The data file is a JS-wrapped copy of the brief with no regeneration note.
evidence.visual_design: Calm system typography, muted greys, a blue link colour and zebra rows on the list (list.jpg). It looks clean but unfinished on detail pages. Drawing text is oversized against hairline geometry. The title-block typography dominates. The Value/Unit columns of the tables shift right and left between sections (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-44_rem_mag.jpg), which looks unaligned.
evidence.layout: The detail page order (heading, facts, drawing, tables) matches the brief. The drawing is followed by an oversized title block. The tables run to 3,500-4,700 px in a single column with lots of empty space between symbol and value. The 9,3 x 74 R α label sits detached at the far right, and the 22 LR L3 label sits left of the drawing. Print fits one page but leaves the right 45% of the sheet empty (print-308_win.jpg). There is no clipping or overlap of text.
evidence.usability: The list is quick to scan; search filters as you type and the family filter combines with it. The list state survives returning from detail (app.js:102). Detail URLs can be bookmarked, unknown keys show a not-found page with a back link, and Print is one click. Finding a value means scrolling a long single-column table list on desktop.
evidence.reception: Reloaders would like the complete data and the drawing generated from the values. Engineers and gunsmiths would spot drafting errors: diameters drawn as one-sided leaders without ⌀, α drawn as a half-angle arc floating beyond the tip on some cases, a 'Scale 1:1' claim that is not true, and a print with tiny tables. That limits trust in a tool meant as a reference.

unmet_requirements: Diameter dimensions (R1, P1, P2, H1, H2, G1, E1) are single-arrow leaders, not dimension lines with arrowheads and extension lines (layout.js:222-235)
Shoulder angle α is drawn as a half-angle arc at apex S, which falls outside the part on 9,3 x 74 R (detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg) and overlaps the bullet on 308
Printed drawing is not at full page width; the sheet is scaled to about 55% and the tables print at about 4 pt (print-308_win.jpg)
Title block always states 'Scale 1:1', which is not the scale shown on screen or in print
No README, CI or decision documentation (maintainability expectations)
strengths: The geometry engine implements nearly every drawing rule exactly: chamfer, rimfire half-round, groove and belt, filleted shoulder through the published points, tangent ogive, heeled bullet, walls, solid head and primer pockets. It has precise unit tests.
Data is shown faithfully: values as published, tolerances in the same cell, angles as D°MM'SS", the symbol mapping, and search across alternative names with comma/point equivalence.
Clean, dependency-free, safe code: escaped SVG markup, no network, a pure module split testable in Node, and solid accessibility basics.
issues: Drafting defects visible to an expert: diameters are one-sided leaders, and α is a half-angle arc at apex S that floats past the bullet tip on 9,3 x 74 R and sits on the bullet on 308.

Print layout scales the whole sheet down to about 55% width: the drawing is not full width, the tables are about 4 pt, and fit depends on a hand-calibrated height estimate with overflow clipping. The title block's 'Scale 1:1' is false.
No README, CI, ADRs or pinned runtime file. The detail page is a very long single column of tables with shifting value columns and oversized drawing labels and title block.
review.verdict: The app builds true-to-scale drawings almost exactly to the brief's geometry rules, presents the data faithfully, and is clean and well tested at the unit level. The dimensioning (one-sided diameter leaders, a misplaced half-angle α, a false scale), the shrunken print layout and the missing project documentation need fixing before it is published to engineers and gunsmiths.
